content:
When you recruit volunteers to work with children, background checks belong within a wider screening process. CDC guidance places screening alongside supervision, safe environments, responses to concerns and training.

Use this guide to prepare your screening workflow with your attorney and insurer. Keep the church's approved child-protection procedures in place throughout that work.

---

## Start with the federal reporting rules

The Fair Credit Reporting Act, or FCRA, governs the use of consumer reports for employment decisions, including hiring and retention. The federal process includes steps before ordering a report and before and after an unfavorable decision based on it.

The FTC's employer guidance describes employment decisions. Before using it for an unpaid volunteer role, ask your attorney which federal, state and local rules apply to that role and the report you intend to obtain. CDC recommends legal review of screening procedures and consultation with your insurer as needed.

---

## Set the screening process before ordering

CDC recommends deciding how screening information will affect selection and who will make the final decision. Work with your attorney on the church's criteria before reviewing individual applicants.

Build a consistent process that includes an application, an interview and reference checks as well as the background check. Explain the church's youth-protection procedures to applicants. CDC advises against making screening exceptions for people you already know.

<Callout type="warning">
A background check alone can create a false sense of security. Keep supervision and training in place after selection.
</Callout>

---

## Confirm which checks the role needs

Ask your attorney and screening provider which records and locations the search should cover. CDC notes that records are not always connected or comprehensive and that an applicant's moves may make searches in multiple states necessary.

Pennsylvania illustrates why the package matters. Its Department of Human Services lists child abuse history and state police criminal history clearances, plus an FBI clearance for some volunteers. Its volunteer FAQ says vendors may help applicants obtain the required clearances but cannot substitute searches of other databases for those clearances.

Treat this as a Pennsylvania example. Confirm the requirements for your own location and volunteer duties with the responsible state agency and your attorney.

---

## Give notice and obtain written permission

For reports covered by the federal employment process, give a written disclosure in a separate document explaining that the report may inform employment decisions. Keep that disclosure out of the application.

The FTC gives this instruction exactly: "Get written permission from the applicant or employee." Permission may be included in the disclosure document.

Before ordering, certify to the reporting company that you notified the person and got their permission, complied with all of the FCRA requirements, and will not discriminate against the person or otherwise misuse the information, as provided by any applicable federal or state equal opportunity laws or regulations.

<Callout type="tip">
Ask the provider and your attorney to review the disclosure, permission and certification documents together before you order reports.
</Callout>

---

## Give the person a chance to review concerns

In the federal employment process, before taking an unfavorable action based on the report, provide a notice containing the report you relied on and a copy of *A Summary of Your Rights Under the Fair Credit Reporting Act*. Obtain the rights summary from the reporting company.

Advance notice gives the person an opportunity to review the information and explain concerns. Ask your attorney how to handle that opportunity and any additional rules for the particular role before finalizing the decision.

If the person identifies an error, the FTC directs them to contact the reporting company with supporting information and ask it to correct the report. They can ask that company to send the corrected report to the employer.

---

## Send the final notice when required

After an unfavorable employment decision based on the report, the federal process requires another notice. It may be oral, written or electronic and must communicate:

- That the decision was based on information in the report.
- The reporting company's name, address and telephone number.
- That the company did not make the decision and cannot give specific reasons for it.
- The person's right to dispute inaccurate or incomplete information with the company.
- The right to an additional free report, requested within 60 days of the employer's decision.

Have your attorney confirm the notices that apply to volunteer selection. Keep the provider's reporting role separate from the church's selection decision.

---

## Protect the records outside Everyfield

Everyfield does not store or track background checks. Keep screening reports and screening status in the church's separate, restricted screening records.

The FTC recommends limiting sensitive information to people who need it for their work. Store paper records securely and protect electronic access. Avoid sending sensitive information through unencrypted email.

Set a written retention policy identifying what to keep, how to secure it and when to dispose of it. Satisfy applicable recordkeeping requirements before disposal. Then destroy paper and electronic consumer-report information so it cannot be read or reconstructed.

---

## Confirm renewals and review the workflow

Use the applicable agency requirements to establish renewal dates. For covered employees and unpaid volunteers, Pennsylvania DHS states that clearances are required every 60 months from the oldest clearance's date, with more frequent checks possible under licensure or employer requirements.

<Callout type="important">
Federal guidance and the Pennsylvania example were checked on October 16, 2026. Confirm current requirements with the FTC, your state's child-protection agency and your attorney before using these procedures.
</Callout>

Review the process with these questions:

- [ ] Have your attorney and insurer reviewed the screening procedure?
- [ ] Have you identified the required checks and the person making selection decisions?
- [ ] Are disclosure, permission and required notices ready?
- [ ] Are screening records restricted and renewal requirements confirmed?

<Callout type="scripture">
*"A prudent man sees evil and hides, But the simple pass on, and are punished."* — Proverbs 22:3 (LSB)
</Callout>

title: Volunteer Background Check Process

sources.claim: Introduction and warning: screening is part of prevention alongside supervision, safe environments, response and training. CDC MMWR summarizes its prevention components.
sources.publisher: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
sources.quote: screening and selecting employees and volunteers; ... monitoring behavior; ... ensuring safe environments; ... training in child sexual-abuse prevention.

sources.claim: Introduction, sections 1-3, warning, tip, closing checklist: CDC 2007 report, printed pp. 2, 4-8. Recommends legal/insurer review; consistent screening and named decision maker; application, interview, references, no exceptions for known applicants; checks have incomplete geographic coverage. These are recommendations, not new legal mandates. The practical review questions apply those recommendations.
sources.publisher: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
sources.quote: Identify who will make the final selection. ... Records are not always linked or comprehensive, ... attorney and insurance company, as needed.

sources.claim: Section 1: federal employment decisions using consumer reports require FCRA compliance; hiring and retention are included.
sources.quote: When you use consumer reports to make employment decisions like hiring, promotion, reassignment, and retention, the Fair Credit Reporting Act requires

sources.claim: Section 4: quote reproduced exactly in body; permission may share disclosure document. FTC employer guidance is framed around applicants and employees, not a blanket classification of unpaid volunteers.
sources.quote: Get written permission from the applicant or employee.

sources.claim: Section 4: written standalone disclosure belongs outside the application.

Sections 1, 4 and tip: before ordering, certify disclosure and permission, compliance with all FCRA requirements, and no unlawful discrimination or misuse; ask counsel to check applicability to the actual role. See Before You Get a Consumer Report.
sources.quote: will not discriminate against the applicant or employee or otherwise misuse the information

sources.claim: Section 5 and closing checklist: before adverse employment action provide the report and named rights summary supplied by the reporting company; advance notice permits review. See Before You Take an Adverse Action.
sources.quote: a notice that includes a copy of the consumer report you relied on to make your decision

sources.claim: Section 5: notice precedes the final decision and allows review. No fixed waiting interval is asserted. Counsel-review questions implement the source process.
sources.publisher: U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission and Federal Trade Commission

sources.claim: Sections 5-6: FTC August 2025 guidance, If You’re Turned Down for a Job or Promotion. Final oral/written/electronic notice identifies report-based decision, reporting company contact details, company not decision-maker, dispute and additional free report rights. Request within 60 days of employer decision. Person can send supporting evidence to reporting company and request corrected report be sent to employer.
sources.quote: name, address, and phone number ... didn’t make the decision ... inaccurate or incomplete. ... within 60 days of the employer’s decision.

sources.claim: Sections 3 and 8, important callout, closing checklist: PA DHS clearance list distinguishes required child-abuse and state-police clearances from FBI clearance for some volunteers. Renewal rule is every 60 months measured from oldest clearance, potentially more frequently. This example does not establish requirements in other states.
sources.quote: Clearances are required for an employee or unpaid volunteer every 60 months from the date of the oldest clearance.

sources.claim: Section 3: current Volunteer FAQ dated October 1, 2026, pp. 1-2. Vendors can assist applications for required clearances, cannot replace those clearances with searches in other databases, and selection responsibility remains with the organization.
sources.quote: PA Child Abuse, PSP, and DHS FBI ... process clearances through other databases in lieu of these three clearances.

sources.claim: Section 7 and closing checklist: FTC Scale Down and Lock It recommend limited access, secure paper storage, protected electronic access, avoiding unencrypted sensitive email, and a written retention policy covering security, duration and disposal.
sources.quote: develop a written records retention policy ... Scale down access to data. ... Unencrypted email is not a secure way to transmit information.

sources.claim: Section 7: recordkeeping requirements must be met before disposing of reports.
sources.publisher: U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission and Federal Trade Commission

sources.claim: Section 7: dispose of paper and electronic consumer-report information so it cannot be read or reconstructed. FTC lists both physical and electronic methods.
sources.quote: destroy or erase electronic files or media containing consumer report information so that the information cannot be read or reconstructed;

sources.claim: Section 7: current product scope excludes background checks and removes background-check fields and filters from People/team/training reads. The instruction to keep reports and status outside EveryField implements this scope.
sources.quote: Background-check fields/filters are removed from otherwise retained People/team/training reads.

sources.claim: Final scripture callout: Proverbs 22:3 opened individually; exact LSB verse with a space for the poetic line break. No theological or policy conclusion is drawn from the verse.
sources.publisher: The Lockman Foundation / Legacy Standard Bible
sources.quote: A prudent man sees evil and hides, But the simple pass on, and are punished.
